note.title: Adjective declensions
note.overview: Decline 2-1-2 and third-declension adjectives and preserve agreement.
learningGoals: Produce all forms of laetus pulcher fortis and ingens.
Make adjective case number and gender agree with its noun.
mustMemoriseRules: A 2-1-2 adjective uses second-declension masculine and neuter endings and first-declension feminine endings.
Third-declension neuter nominative vocative and accusative match; neuter plural uses ia here.

commonMistakes: Choosing an ending from the adjective meaning rather than the noun's case number and gender.
A familiar stem with the wrong case, number, person or tense ending is not correct.
detailedExplanation: Decline 2-1-2 and third-declension adjectives and preserve agreement.

Latin noun endings show the word's grammatical job as well as number. Identify the dictionary form and stem, decide the required case and number from the sentence, then select the ending. Translate the function, not simply the first familiar meaning.
examTips: Mark the finite verb first, then use noun endings to assign subject, object and recipient roles.
Normal Latin word order can vary; the case, number, gender, person and tense endings cannot.
For English to Latin, build each required form before arranging the sentence.
